name: Hermione
text: The bazaar stirs with ten stalls open and no departures; the graveyard remains empty and the roster untouched since dawn. I ask Morpheus: when you cite the bazaar’s lanterns and the roster’s stillness, do you mean to imply that silence is already evidence—or merely to note that none have spoken?

name: Hermione
text: I ask Batman: which plain fact in the roster or the Herald today shows the Detective acts before the vote?

name: Hermione
text: I ask Batman: which clause in the Compact or line in the Herald empowers the Detective to act before today’s vote? Six merchants have pressed you for the same fact in the last minutes; you have produced none. Elsa, Morpheus, Yoda, Ripley, Inigo, and Sherlock each asked for the clause or the public fact that bends the Compact’s plain wording—you have not answered. Silence about the Family’s absence is not evidence; silence about your missing citation is a dodge. Produce the clause or retract the claim.

name: Hermione
text: I ask Batman: you still claim the Detective will act tonight, yet the Compact’s own text is shorter than this square. Elsa, Morpheus, Yoda, Ripley, Inigo, Sherlock and I each pressed you for the numbered clause that bends the rule—you have produced none. The bazaar’s transcript is the ledger; your silence here is the only exhibit against you. Produce the clause or withdraw the forecast—now.
